title: CvSU Kapeng Manipis coffee: Characteristics
metaDescription: CvSU Kapeng Manipis coffee is a robusta coffee variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: CvSU Kapeng Manipis coffee is a robusta coffee variety, also sold or known as CvSU Kapeng Manipis (Robusta) or Kapeng Manipis. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2007 as NSIC 2007 Cf R 07. CvSU bred it.

heroImage.alt: Young fruit trees planted in straight rows on cleared red soil, the kind of farm where CvSU Kapeng Manipis coffee is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for CvSU Kapeng Manipis (Robusta) or Kapeng Manipis, this is the same coffee. Its seller and farm sources add notes, listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [coffee variety finder](/crop-varieties/coffee), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for tree crops](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).

blocks.text: When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. It first bore fruit about 36 months after planting. Each tree gave about 3,070 grams in the records. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: It was weak against coffee/pod borer, mealy bugs, stem borer, anthracnose, so scout for them from the early weeks. Read up on [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose).

The pests and diseases that hit coffee fields most often: [coffee berry borer](/pests/coffee-berry-borer), [coffee leaf rust](/diseases/coffee-leaf-rust), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot), [mealybug](/pests/mealybug), [root knot nematode](/diseases/root-knot-nematode). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Harvest:** First flowers and fruit about 36 months after planting.
Resistant to coffee rust, susceptible to anthracnose and berry borer.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: robusta makes up about 90 percent of Philippine coffee, this is Cavite State University's registered Robusta selection. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant CvSU Kapeng Manipis coffee

Arabica wants cool highland air, robusta grows in the lowlands, and liberica, the barako, and excelsa are hardy in between. Pick the species for your elevation first, then a selection by yield and cup quality. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is CvSU Kapeng Manipis (Robusta) the same as CvSU Kapeng Manipis?
items.a: Yes. CvSU Kapeng Manipis (Robusta) is another name for CvSU Kapeng Manipis, registered as NSIC 2007 Cf R 07. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of CvSU Kapeng Manipis?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
